references.text: The Preacher warns that whoever loves money will never be satisfied with money – a parallel to Jesus' warning against greed and the belief that abundance gives life ([ref:Eccles 5:10|Ecclesiastes 5:10]).
Whoever trusts in riches will fall – a wisdom admonition underlying Jesus' words that life does not depend on what one owns ([ref:Prov 11:4|Proverbs 11:4]).
The Proverbs warn against striving for wealth, for it can vanish suddenly – this is the same fundamental attitude Jesus warns against ([ref:Prov 23:4-5|Proverbs 23:4-5]).
A ruler who lacks understanding is a great oppressor, but whoever hates dishonest gain will live long – a proverb linking greed to the value of life ([ref:Prov 28:16|Proverbs 28:16]).

Paul warns that those who want to be rich fall into temptation and a trap, for the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil – an admonition reflecting Jesus' warning against greed ([ref:1 Tim 6:9-10|1 Timothy 6:9-10]).

The author of Hebrews urges believers to keep their lives free from the love of money and to be content with what they have – the same thought as Jesus' warning in this verse ([ref:Heb 13:5|Hebrews 13:5]).
Paul mentions greed (πλεονεξία) as something that should not even be named among the saints, using the same word Jesus uses in his warning ([ref:Eph 5:3|Ephesians 5:3]).
Paul admonishes the Colossians to put to death greed, which is idolatry – a strong parallel to Jesus' warning against all kinds of greed ([ref:Col 3:5|Colossians 3:5]).
Jesus immediately after this warning tells the parable of the rich farmer, illustrating that life does not consist in an abundance of possessions ([ref:Luke 12:16-21|Luke 12:16-21]).
Jesus says that no servant can serve two masters, and that one cannot serve both God and Mammon – an elaboration on the warning against greed ([ref:Luke 16:13|Luke 16:13]).

Job declares that he has not put his trust in gold or rejoiced over his great wealth – an attitude consistent with Jesus' teaching that life does not depend on one's possessions ([ref:Job 31:24-25|Job 31:24-25]).
The psalmist warns against setting one's heart on riches even if they increase – a direct parallel to Jesus' admonition not to build life on what one owns ([ref:Ps 62:11|Psalms 62:11]).
